transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

I came in because I can’t stop thinking about how I look, especially my hairline and my face. At work, under the restaurant lights, I feel like I look old and kind of strange. My coworkers say they don’t notice anything, but I still see it, and it’s been really hard to get it out of my head.
Does this concern about your appearance make it hard for you to focus on your work, interact with others, or cause you a lot of emotional distress?

Yes. It’s gotten bad enough that I’ve been written up at the restaurant because I’m late or I miss shifts. And I’ve stopped going to things like staff photos, gallery events, even hikes, because I just can’t handle being seen looking that way. It’s embarrassing, and it really gets in the way.
Can you describe more about what exactly bothers you regarding your hairline and face? Do you see it as a defect or flaw that others might not notice?

It’s mostly my hairline and my face, yeah. I look at myself and I feel like my hairline makes me look old, and under the restaurant lights my face just looks strange to me. I know other people say they don’t notice it, like my coworkers tell me they can’t see what I’m talking about, but to me it feels really obvious. I keep seeing it as a flaw.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, camouflaging your hairline, or seeking reassurance, because of your concerns about how you look?

Yes. Before a shift I’ll keep going into the bathroom to check the mirror, over and over. I take pictures on my phone from different angles to see how bad it looks, and I keep combing my hair forward to cover the hairline. Then I start thinking through how guests are going to see me, and I can get so stuck on it that I’m late going out front, or I’m too worked up to do it.
